source: NCERT Class VII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Metals and Non-metals
points: Materials are broadly grouped into **metals** and **non-metals** based on their properties.
**Metals** — iron, copper, aluminium, gold, silver, zinc.

sub: **Lustrous** (shiny), **hard**, **malleable** (can be beaten into sheets), **ductile** (drawn into wires).
**Good conductors** of heat and electricity; **sonorous** (make a ringing sound); usually **solid** (except mercury, a liquid).
**Poor conductors** (except **graphite**, which conducts); may be solid, liquid or gas.

sections.heading: 3. Chemical Properties
points: **Metals + oxygen → basic oxides** (e.g. iron oxide, magnesium oxide) → turn red litmus blue.
**Non-metals + oxygen → acidic oxides** (e.g. carbon dioxide, sulphur dioxide) → turn blue litmus red.
**Metals react with acids** to release **hydrogen gas**; most non-metals do not.
Some metals react with water (sodium reacts vigorously).

sections.heading: 4. Uses
points: **Metals:** machinery, wires (copper), utensils, construction, coins, jewellery (gold/silver).
**Non-metals:** oxygen (breathing), nitrogen (fertilisers), carbon (fuel/graphite pencils), iodine (medicine/antiseptic), chlorine (water treatment).
**Exceptions to remember:** **mercury** = liquid metal; **graphite** = non-metal that conducts electricity.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Metals: lustrous, hard, malleable, ductile, sonorous, good conductors (usually solid).
Non-metals: dull, brittle, poor conductors (except graphite); may be solid/liquid/gas.
Metal oxides = basic; non-metal oxides = acidic.
Exceptions: mercury = liquid metal; graphite = conducting non-metal.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Mercury** is a **metal** but is **liquid** at room temperature.
**Graphite** is a **non-metal** that **conducts electricity** (used in pencils/electrodes).
**Metal oxides are basic**; **non-metal oxides are acidic** — don't swap.
**Malleable** = beaten into sheets; **ductile** = drawn into wires.
